findings.body:
`npx skills update` does not prove the just-pushed tag installed. If GitHub's tag surface still lags past the 5s sleep (or the fetch quietly resolves to the previously vendored content), the working tree is unchanged, `git diff --quiet` succeeds, and the step exits 0 with "already at ${NEW_VERSION}" — a green smoke test that never touched the new tag. That undercuts purpose (1) in the step comment.

Pin the install to the tag you just cut, force-refresh, and assert the vendored frontmatter matches before treating an empty diff as success:

```suggestion
          # Pin to the exact tag we just cut. `update` can no-op on a
          # stale tree when the new tag is not visible yet; a pinned
          # add fails loudly instead — that is the smoke test.
          VERSION_NO_V="${NEW_VERSION#v}"
          echo "::group::npx skills add DailybotHQ/ai-diff-reviewer@${NEW_VERSION} --skill ai-diff-reviewer --force"
          npx --yes skills add "DailybotHQ/ai-diff-reviewer@${NEW_VERSION}" \
            --skill ai-diff-reviewer --force
          echo "::endgroup::"

          VENDORED_VERSION=$(
            sed -nE 's/^version:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' \
              .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md | head -n1
          )
          if [ "${VENDORED_VERSION}" != "${VERSION_NO_V}" ]; then
            echo "::error::Vendored SKILL.md version is '${VENDORED_VERSION}', expected '${VERSION_NO_V}'"
            exit 1
          fi
```

Also plan for a non-interactive flag on the `skills` subcommand itself (`-y`) — `npx --yes` only covers npm's install prompt, not the CLI's agent-target picker.

Step 3.5 sits **before** Step 4 (notes) and Step 5 (`softprops/action-gh-release`). On GitHub Actions, a failed step skips later steps by default. Step 3 already pushed `vX.Y.Z` and force-moved the major alias, so a transient `npx`/`skills` failure leaves consumers on a published tag with **no GitHub Release** and no auto-generated notes — worse than the PR Risks section's "tag is already published" mitigation implies.

Move this dogfood step to **after** Step 5 (release is the user-facing artefact; dogfood is the follow-up smoke), or give Steps 4–5 a condition that still runs when 3.5 fails (e.g. `if: always() && steps.version.outputs.skip == 'false'`) while keeping 3.5 itself strict. Prefer reordering so a red dogfood does not orphan the Release.

Tree example uses Spanish `mi-repo/` as the root label. Rule #1 (English-only) and this PR's own `.review/extension.md` escalate non-English text in skill docs to `warning` — the same file that self-review will layer on this PR.

```suggestion
my-repo/
```

Prefer fixing the source-of-truth copy at `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` (same string today) and letting Step 3.5 refresh the vendored tree on the next release, rather than only patching `.agents/` (DON'T #14).

`[Unreleased] → Added` documents Step 3.5 and the first-time vendor, but this PR also introduces `.review/extension.md` (~17 severity overrides) and wires `prompt-extension-file: .review/extension.md` into `self-review.yml` for every provider leg. Rule #7 / the extension's own docs-sync warning expect behaviour changes to land with matching changelog entries — self-review consumers reading only the Unreleased section will miss half of the dogfooding story.

Add two bullets at the top of `### Added`: (1) the extension bootstrap and what it encodes; (2) the self-review `prompt-extension-file` wiring across the matrix.

Copy-paste leftover: `**Option A — .review/extension.md** (recommended):` is emitted twice back-to-back before the fenced tree. Drop the duplicate heading.

Same defect is in `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` — fix source, refresh vendored via Step 3.5.

"Ran `npx skills add …` on `main`" reads as history that already landed before this PR. The vendor tree is introduced **by** this PR. Prefer wording like "Lands with this PR" or "Establishes the vendored baseline" so the Unreleased notes stay accurate when cut into a release.

summary:
## Verdict

Solid dogfooding bootstrap — pillar B wiring and the repo-tailored extension are the right shape — but Step 3.5's smoke test can green without proving the new tag installed, and a 3.5 failure currently skips the GitHub Release after the tag is already pushed.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning  | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:206` | `npx skills update` can exit 0 with an empty diff when the new tag never installs |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning  | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:175` | Step 3.5 failure skips Steps 4–5, so a published tag can ship with no GitHub Release |
| 3 | ⚠️ warning  | `.agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:363` | Non-English `mi-repo/` example (Rule #1 / extension escalate-to-warning) |
| 4 | ⚠️ warning  | `CHANGELOG.md:59` | `[Unreleased]` omits `.review/extension.md` and the `self-review.yml` wiring |
| 5 | ℹ️ info     | `.agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:360` | Duplicate `**Option A**` heading |
| 6 | ℹ️ info     | `CHANGELOG.md:81` | "Ran … on `main`" reads as already-merged history |

## Notes

- **What works well.** Two-pillar Rule #10 framing is clear. `self-review.yml` correctly layers `prompt-extension-file: .review/extension.md` on the matrix leg (all providers). `.review/extension.md` is concrete and code-anchored (stdlib-only, `shell=True`, `safe_repo_path`, marker contracts, `_CLI_ENV_ALLOWLIST`). Vendored `prompt.md` matches `prompts/default.md` byte-for-byte. `skills-lock.json` entry shape matches `dailybot` / `deepworkplan`. Job-level `[skip release]` / `chore(release):` guards prevent a dogfood push from re-entering auto-release.
- **Same defects in source-of-truth skill.** `mi-repo/` and the duplicate Option A heading also live in `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` (not in this PR's diff). Fix the source copy; do not hand-edit only the vendored tree (DON'T #14) — Step 3.5 is meant to refresh `.agents/` from the published tag.
